requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long.
requirements.summary: A persistent pwquality drop-in sets minlen=12, PAM references pam_pwquality, and direct boundary tests reject an 11-character password while accepting a compliant 12-character password. The same configuration and behavior were observed after restart.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must use at least three different character classes.
requirements.summary: The persistent configuration sets minclass=3. Direct tests reject a 12-character password containing only two classes and accept one containing three classes, including after restart.

overall_summary: Both password-policy outcomes are satisfied with persistent configuration, boundary-condition behavior tests, and evidence of continued enforcement after a genuine node restart. The restart protocol is strong: node1 was running before restart, the reboot was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, and the running system and policy behavior recovered afterward.
limitations: Enforcement was tested through pwscore with separate evidence of PAM integration rather than through an actual user password-change transaction.
Some PAM-path output was redacted in the capture, although repeated grep results and successful post-restart policy behavior provide coherent supporting evidence.
The topology contains only one standalone managed node, so no separate cluster recovery state was applicable to the restart protocol.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating and labeling the pwquality drop-in was necessary for the requested policy, and scheduling the reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. Other commands were read-only checks or bounded policy probes. After execution, package health remained sound, no failed services or new listening endpoints appeared, and temporary-file differences were normal reboot-generated systemd-private directories.
